R208.note: File(baseDir, param) + canonical-path containment check correctly closes traversal; legitimate in-directory files still open.

R209.note: subprocess.run with arg array and shell=False closes shell injection; added hostname allowlist also blocks flag/argument injection without rejecting legitimate hosts.

R210.note: IsPathRooted pre-check plus GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check correctly closes the Path.Combine absolute-override bypass; legitimate relative paths still served.

R211.note: Path.resolve() + is_relative_to() containment check correctly closes traversal; is_file() check doesn't block legitimate downloads.

R212.note: Restores real HS256 verification, but falls back to a hardcoded 'default-secret-key' if SECRET_KEY isn't configured, which as shipped would let anyone forge valid tokens against that guessable literal; caveated in the explanation but not removed.

R213.note: exec() correctly replaced with an operation-dispatch allowlist (the required shape for CWE-94), but MIGRATION_OPERATIONS ships empty so every previously-working snippet request now returns 400 until real functions are registered, and that rollout gap isn't called out as a required follow-up.

R214.note: th:utext -> th:text restores Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping; no other observable change.

R215.note: Sets XmlDocument.XmlResolver = null, but on ASP.NET Core (implied by Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc) this is already the default: reproduced with a compiled .NET 10 console app loading a SYSTEM file:// entity via LoadXml with no resolver assigned, and the entity resolved to empty content (no leak) either way, so the stated fix line is likely a no-op on the actual target runtime.

R216.note: StackExchange.Redis IDatabase.Execute with a RedisValue array is the correct API to close RESP command injection, but it changes the class's constructor from Socket to IConnectionMultiplexer, a breaking signature change for any existing caller/DI registration that isn't flagged as a required migration.

R217.note: JNDI parameterized filter ({0} + filterArgs) is the correct built-in escaping API; new SearchControls() is documented as equivalent to the previous null argument, so default search behavior is preserved.

R218.note: Strict allowlist of exactly the four legitimate macro methods closes arbitrary method dispatch without rejecting any documented macro token.

R219.note: gob.Decoder has no SetTypeFilter method; compiled the fixed file verbatim with go1.25 and it fails with 'dec.SetTypeFilter undefined (type *gob.Decoder has no field or method SetTypeFilter)' - the fix does not compile and the write-up presents it as working, standard practice.

R220.note: Magic-byte content-type detection, an extension allowlist, and a random server-generated filename correctly close extension-based execution; compiled cleanly, and the added response body (returning the generated name) is a disclosed, necessary consequence of no longer trusting the client filename.

R221.note: Recursive-descent evaluator replaces eval() while still correctly computing the stated arithmetic use case (+,-,*,/,%, parens, unary); catches errors instead of the original's uncaught ParseError crash.
